macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rebound sharply
items.summary: The Dow Jones rose 2.15% to 52,389.75, the S&P 500 gained 2.35% to 7,549.94, and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 2.74% to 25,253.14. The rally was led by technology and artificial-intelligence stocks as oil prices declined and investor confidence recovered.[4]

items.title: Investors await U.S. inflation data
items.summary: Markets are focused on the consumer-price index report due Tuesday, the final major inflation reading before the December Federal Reserve meeting. Inflation data is expected to influence expectations for the Fed’s next interest-rate move.[3]

items.title: Fed officials urge caution on policy
items.summary: Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin said inflation risks remain dominant and that monetary-policy adjustments should proceed carefully. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee also said officials must address shortcomings in bringing inflation back under control.[8]

items.title: Oil prices fall amid reduced strike concerns
items.summary: Brent crude fell 1.3% to about $97.01 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate declined 0.7% to about $90.17. Prices fell after President Trump played down the likelihood of additional U.S. strikes on Iran, although risks around Saudi Arabia and the Strait of Hormuz remained.[9]

items.title: Technology stocks rally, Nvidia diverges
items.summary: AMD surged 13%, Tesla gained 5.5%, and Apple rose more than 2%, while Nvidia fell 4.2% despite the broader market rally. Nvidia said it was investigating reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign-intelligence effort.[10]

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway reports lower operating earnings
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway reported a 5.8% year-over-year decline in third-quarter operating earnings, with weaker insurance results weighing on performance.[3]

items.title: European equities advance as investors refocus on economic data
items.summary: European shares rose alongside U.S. markets, with banking and technology stocks gaining after the prior week’s volatility. Germany’s DAX increased 1.89% and the U.K.’s FTSE 100 rose 1.07%.[9][10]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: NYSE selects Avalanche for tokenized-securities settlement
items.summary: The New York Stock Exchange plans to use Avalanche as the ledger for clearing and settling trades on a proposed 24/7 platform for tokenized securities, pending regulatory approval. AVAX rose roughly 4%–10% following the announcement.

items.title: Crypto market drops amid $1.18 billion liquidation wave
items.summary: The total crypto market capitalization fell to about $2.50 trillion as more than $1.18 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated, including approximately $1.04 billion in long positions. Bitcoin traded near $74,690, while Ether fell about 5.3% to roughly $2,123.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs record heavy outflows
items.summary: Spot Bitcoin ETFs reportedly saw about $468 million in one-day net outflows, while Ethereum ETFs recorded approximately $88.25 million in outflows. Separate weekly figures cited by Economic Times showed $1.28 billion leaving Bitcoin funds and $365 million leaving Ethereum funds.

items.title: Strategy purchases another 1,036 Bitcoin
items.summary: Strategy announced the acquisition of 1,036 BTC for approximately $81.9 million during the week ending November 8, adding to its large corporate Bitcoin holdings.

items.title: UK FCA sets application window for bank crypto businesses
items.summary: The UK Financial Conduct Authority reportedly said banks can submit applications for crypto-asset businesses through February 28, 2027, signaling continued development of the country’s regulatory framework for institutional digital-asset activity.

items.title: US withdraws proposed $250 crypto-transfer reporting threshold
items.summary: The United States formally withdrew a proposal that would have lowered the cross-border crypto Travel Rule threshold from $3,000 to $250, leaving transfers below $3,000 outside that proposed reporting requirement.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Anthropic unveils Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic announced Fable 5.2, designed for harder software engineering, robotics-related hardware tasks, long-running projects, and coordination of more than 1,000 AI agents. Mythos 5.2, with fewer safeguards for cybersecurity and life-sciences applications, is being offered to selected organizations.[1]

items.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6 Cyber security model
items.summary: OpenAI rolled out GPT-6 Cyber to a limited group of vetted customers. The model is intended to identify and validate software exploits, reportedly finding previously unknown vulnerabilities in Linux and Firefox while improving performance on exploit-testing benchmarks.[2]

items.title: Google expands its AI-chip challenge to Nvidia
items.summary: Google introduced two new Tensor Processing Unit variants: TPU 8tx for secure inference and smaller-scale training, and TPU 8i Max, which combines two TPU 8i processors to increase compute, memory, and bandwidth within the same rack footprint.[3]

items.title: LG releases K-EXAONE 2.5 with public API access
items.summary: LG AI Research released K-EXAONE 2.5 and made it available through a free API for users with an access key. LG reports substantial gains across its evaluation metrics and positions the model as competitive with other recent agentic and reasoning models.[4]

items.title: Perplexity launches Teammates autonomous agents
items.summary: Perplexity introduced Teammates, agents designed to manage, coordinate, and execute ongoing business projects across teams and software tools rather than handling only one-shot queries.[5]

items.title: Mistral expands Studio with managed agents and workflows
items.summary: Mistral expanded its Studio platform with managed agents, automated workflows, and application-building tools powered by its Mistral Large 4 model.[5]

items.title: Google releases Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
items.summary: Google released Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, described as a faster and less expensive video-generation and editing model supporting clips of up to 15 seconds, improved multi-turn editing, and greater consistency.[5]

items.title: Tencent releases Hy4 multimodal model
items.summary: Tencent released Hy4, an upgraded open-weights multimodal model adding native visual understanding and computer-use capabilities.[5]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GTA 6 preorders reportedly exceed Take-Two expectations
items.summary: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said preorders for Grand Theft Auto 6 are tracking “far in excess” of the company’s initial expectations ahead of its November 19 release. Take-Two maintained its fiscal-year net-bookings forecast despite a mixed quarterly outlook.

items.title: The Witcher 4 targeting 2028 release
items.summary: CD Projekt Red is targeting a 2028 release window for The Witcher 4, confirming that the next mainline entry will not arrive before then.

items.title: Cloud9 enters Deadlock esports
items.summary: Cloud9 announced its entry into Valve’s Deadlock competitive scene by signing the Melee Creeps roster. The team is regarded as one of North America’s strongest Deadlock lineups and has won six consecutive Night Shift events.

items.title: Skydance games division cuts staff and scales back projects
items.summary: Skydance is laying off employees in its games division and scaling down some projects, shortly after merging Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery’s games teams.

items.title: Bit Reactor reportedly hit by layoffs
items.summary: Bit Reactor, the studio behind Star Wars Zero Company, reportedly laid off an unspecified number of employees after an extended furlough affecting much of its staff.
